## Goal

The same artifact source renders inline in chat hosts as an MCP App, persisting through the local server, with a full-page URL always offered.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| MC-02 | MCP Apps export: one artifact compiles to a single-file `ui://` resource with declared CSP, mapped theme variables and a bridge transport; the full-page URL is always offered | I, X | ext-apps reference host renders the export; fields, submit and actions round-trip; CSP and variables declared; URL fallback offered; external: Claude Desktop and VS Code |
| MC-03 | Features unavailable inside chat iframes degrade explicitly | B | Each unavailable feature shows its explicit message in the MCP App (browser) |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- the MCP App exporter as a first-party plugin on the exporter contract (a single-file `ui://` resource, declared CSP, token-to-host-context variable mapping);
- the client runtime's MCP Apps transport with app-only tools;
- explicit degradation for unavailable features;
- `artifact_open` returning the app plus the URL fallback;
- persistence through the remote MCP server (WP-30) in cloud chat hosts, replacing D61's "until then" message (D116); local hosts are unchanged.

Design detail for this package:

- Open issues on the `WP-17` milestone (work-package protocol §2, M41), each fixed at its root with a test as strict as before, or closed with evidence: #139 (an owner's log once held two imported hosted submissions out of the server's order: the hosted outbox's in-order deliveries and the follow's import of a submission it doesn't hold yet both append `submission.created`; decide whether the follow waits for deliveries to catch up or the order that counts is each import's hosted cursor, `origin.cursor`, and hold RM-08's order to it). It touches what this package's persistence through the remote MCP server goes through: a hosted home's submissions reaching their owner.
- From WP-15 (D164): `artifact_open` returns the default link (`view/default`) or a new one (`view/url`); add the `ui://mostra/view/<versionId>` resource to its result additively, and register the app-only tools (`visibility: ["app"]`) on the same `createMcpServerFactory`, so the local server (`mostra mcp`) and WP-30's remote one serve them alike.
- From WP-07 (D111): the `mcp-app` export writes `<meta name="mostra-target" content="mcp-app">`; `mountRoutes` then uses memory history, as `pages.spec.ts` checks on a marked build: run it on the real exporter's output (AU-09). The MCP Apps transport implements `packages/react/src/runtime/transport.ts`'s `Transport` over the app-only tools; `boot.ts` currently starts mcp-app pages in local mode until it exists.
- Exporter plugin: single-file `ui://` resource, declared CSP, token-to-host variable mapping.
- Client runtime MCP Apps transport over app-only tools; memory routing.
- Explicit degradation messages (MC-03).
- In cloud chat hosts, exported apps persist drafts, submissions and actions through WP-30's remote MCP server (D116), which replaces D61's "until then" message; under local hosts nothing changes. WP-30 closed MC-04 up to the inline round trip (its check boundary): repeat MC-04's external check inline in claude.ai and ChatGPT through the remote MCP server, and extend WP-30's MC-04 evidence row with the result.
- From WP-30 (D167 item 20): the project's test deployment (`docs/agents/test-deployment.md`) is where MC-04's inline check runs: refresh it with this package's candidate, then an agent in claude.ai creates, opens inline, answers and submits an artifact through the remote MCP server; ChatGPT's check waits for a Business workspace Mirza arranges (M60). The playbook says when the deployment is retired.
